High-level ask: we want a pricing ladder that rewards growth but keeps our effective rate predictable for forecasting. Our initial preference is for marginal pricing (we pay the marginal discounted rate above each breakpoint) because it maps to our internal cost models, but we want a soft cap on retro credits (can't go negative beyond X% of committed spend) and quarterly true-ups to match seasonality.

Jamie —

Appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet. I attached a short examples doc (redwood_rate_examples_v2.pdf) that walks through two canonical approaches we use when structuring per-token volume discounts:

1) Marginal ladder (preferred for high-variance growth): each breakpoint sets a marginal per-token rate that only applies to tokens in that band. Forecast-friendly for product teams that model incremental usage.

2) Blended band (preferred for simple billing): an effective blended rate that results from summing spend across bands and dividing by total tokens. Easier for accounting but can hide marginal economics.

Key commercial guardrails we typically propose: quarterly true-up with a single carry-forward period (next quarter only), a cap on retro credits at 25% of committed spend per quarter, and a 90-day notice for early termination with a pro-rated clawback on unused committed credits. We can flex those depending on seatbelt sizing.

Ben — looping you and Laura in for the math and billing cadence detail — can you draft the two sample scenarios against Aurea's bands and include sample invoices?

Jamie — does your team lean toward monthly invoices with quarterly true-ups or a single quarterly invoice that reconciles usage? Either is workable; we just want to make sure your accounting team is comfortable.

Cheers,
Diego

Jamie / Diego —

Attached are two worked examples inline below based on Aurea's bands in the spreadsheet. I kept the numbers round to make the tradeoffs obvious.

Scenario assumptions (from Aurea sheet): total committed band = 6 billion tokens over Q3 (split forecast: 0.8B, 1.2B, 4.0B by month).

Option 1 — Marginal ladder (example marginal rates):
- Band A (0–1B): $0.000020 / token
- Band B (1B–5B): $0.000015 / token
- Band C (5B+): $0.000012 / token

Billing math (marginal): pay each token at the band it falls into. If Aurea uses 6B tokens, invoice = (1B * .000020) + (4B * .000015) + (1B * .000012) = $20k + $60k + $12k = $92k => effective blended = $0.00001533

Option 2 — Blended effective rate (one-step price):
- Effective blended rate if 6B tokens and target blended = $0.0000155 => invoice = 6B * .0000155 = $93k (a slightly higher bill but simpler monthly accounting).

True-up / carry rules (proposal):
- Monthly invoicing for actual usage; quarterly true-up to compare committed band vs actual.
- If shortfall relative to committed band, customer can carry forward up to 1 quarter. After that, unfulfilled committed spend converts to an invoice at the standard retail rate (no discount) subject to a retro-credit cap.
- Retro-credit cap: quarter-level cap of 25% of committed discount value (we can move to 20% for larger deals).

Questions for Aurea:
- Would you accept marginal pricing if we include a 25% retro-credit cap and quarterly true-up?
- Do you prefer an automatic carry-forward or an explicit opt-in each quarter?

Laura, can you confirm the invoicing cadence implications (AR follow-up, invoice format) — are there any legal/regulatory items we should flag for Aurea?

—Ben
Head of Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Ben / Diego —

Thanks, this is very helpful and clear. Aurea's finance team reviewed both options and a marginal ladder with a quarterly true-up fits our internal forecasting best. A couple of items from our side:

- We accept the marginal ladder structure provided the retro-credit cap is 30% of the committed discount value (we'll accept 25% only if the minimum committed spend is increased by 15%).
- Quarterly true-ups are fine; we prefer monthly invoicing + quarterly reconciliation so our ops team has visibility.
- We need a hard limit on retro liability in case of an unexpected downturn. Proposal: no carry-back beyond one quarter and an overall downside cap of 30% of the quarter's committed discount (aligns with retro-credit cap item above).
- Please include a short SOW addendum about early termination protections — we will not accept open-ended clawbacks beyond 12 months post-termination.

Attaching our usage forecast to help with the billing schedule (Aurea_usage_forecast_2028Q3.csv). Jamie
